# Nexus

> Connect your agents once. Link your services once.

Nexus sits between AI coding agents and the services they use. It works out which
project an agent is in and sends each call to that project's own account and resource,
so an agent working on one project can't reach another project's services. Made for one
developer running several agents (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode) across several projects.
Platforms: Linux, macOS and Windows (alpha). Needs Node.js 20.10 or newer.

## How it works

Agent → Project → Account → Resource

1. The agent asks Nexus for a service. It doesn't choose the project or the keys.
2. Nexus finds the project, then the account and resource bound to it. If it can't tell,
   or the project isn't registered, it refuses before any call is made.
3. Nexus makes the call with that account's login. The agent never sees the key.

Setup in the app has three steps: pick the project folder, connect an agent (one click
writes the agent's MCP config in the project, with a backup), then unlock Nexus and watch
the agent's first real call arrive. Nexus starts locked and refuses agent calls until
it is unlocked.

## What is covered

- Built in: Supabase (held to one project) and GitHub (held to one repository), signed in
  through the browser with the user's own account.
- Through their own sign-in: Neon, PlanetScale, Airtable, GitLab, Vercel, Cloudflare,
  Netlify, Railway, Sentry, PostHog, Mixpanel, Stripe, PayPal, Resend, Linear, Jira,
  Notion, Confluence, Figma, Hugging Face, Cloudinary, Webflow, Sanity and Zapier.
  Vercel and Figma only accept MCP apps they have approved; Nexus is not approved yet.
  Some of these can be limited to one project, site or base; the rest are kept to the
  right account only, so use one account per project for those.
- Any other service with a public MCP address, added by name and address.
- Read-only by default: Nexus passes only actions a service marks read-only. Safe writes
  can be allowed per binding, never in production.
- Each project keeps a secret-free `.nexus/project.json`. Logins stay in the computer's
  keychain.
- All agents connect to one local Nexus over HTTP. Claude Code and OpenCode report their
  folder to Nexus. Codex doesn't, so its folder is pinned in its config. If an agent
  reports nothing, Nexus refuses.
- A live map of agents, projects and accounts, plus a local activity log without keys.

## What it is not

- Not a password manager, a company governance tool, or a file sandbox.
- It can't see or stop anything an agent does without going through Nexus.
- An agent that can run shell commands as the user could edit Nexus's settings files.
- Guard (approving risky actions one by one) may come later. It is not built.

## Status

Alpha. Claude Code has been run end to end through Nexus; Codex and OpenCode connect the
same way but haven't had a full real session yet. Linux is tested most; macOS and Windows
builds are new. Supabase, GitHub and Notion have been signed in and used live.

## Pricing

The alpha is free. Later: Free up to 2 projects; Pro about $10–12 a month or $99 a year;
Team/Agency later. Prices may change.
